methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $9M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Infinite Machine is a seed-stage transportation company founded by Joseph Cohen and Eddie Cohen that has raised $9.3M to date. The transportation sector peer set includes six private companies—notably Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Navier, and EarthGrid—though no public comparables exist. A narrower peer-median approach proved infeasible; no same-stage or adjacent-stage transportation companies with sufficient data overlap were available to support a reliable multiple.

Stage-progression analysis was the applicable triangulation method. Using $9.3M in total capital raised as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 2.5x multiplier for progression from seed to next stage yields an implied valuation of $23M. This method reflects observed step-ups in early-stage transportation financings, though with limited precedent in the immediate peer cohort.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $20M (low) to $27M (high), with a median point of $23M. This range rests primarily on a single method, which represents a key analytical constraint. Downside risk centers on the absence of tighter peer comparables and the seed-stage company's early operational profile. Upside hinges on capital efficiency metrics and competitive positioning within the transportation tech landscape—data points that were not available for this analysis. Additional disclosure of revenue traction, unit economics, or customer pipeline would materially refine this estimate.
